mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Vietnamese consular legalization; Vietnamese-language sworn translation by Ministry of Justice-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registrar or corporate registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all UBOs, directors, legal representatives and foreign institution shareholders. Screening must cover the OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN Lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, the UK consolidated list, domestic State Bank of Viet Nam / Ministry of Public Security actions, and a commercial world-check or equivalent database for politically exposed persons (PEPs), adverse media and negative regulatory history. Longitudinal screening must continue during the incorporation period and be refreshed at least every 30 days; any direct hit, beneficial-ownership ambiguity or unexplained source-of-funds inconsistency blocks filing and triggers a suspicious transaction report to the Financial Intelligence Unit (State Bank of Viet Nam).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) — https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn, under the Agency for Business Registration, Ministry of Planning and Investment, and the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official legal name must be entered in Vietnamese using the Vietnamese alphabet and diacritics. It must include the legal-form suffix 'Công ty Trách nhiệm hữu hạn' or the accepted abbreviation 'Công ty TNHH'. A foreign-origin commercial name may be transliterated phonetically into Vietnamese; an additional English or other foreign-language name may be shown only after the Vietnamese name and must not be harmful to national sovereignty, historical traditions, cultural identity or public morality. The proposed name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered enterprise, pending application, or protected trade mark, and it must contain at least one distinctive element beyond the legal-form suffix. Names consisting only of numerals, diacritic-free unpronounceable strings or prohibited administrative/socialist-state terms are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bộ, Ủy ban, Hội đồng nhân dân (Ministry, Committee, People's Council)
Việt Nam / Vietnamese (when used in a way that falsely implies state authority, or used as sole entity name)
Ngân hàng (bank) — prior license and State Bank of Viet Nam approval required
Bảo hiểm (insurance) — prior license and Ministry of Finance approval required
Chứng khoán (securities) — prior license and State Securities Commission approval required
Ma túy, cờ bạc, lừa đảo and other words violating statutory prohibition or social ethics
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the provincial DPI issues a written notice stating the legal ground. The applicant may (1) correct and resubmit the proposed name on the National Business Registration Portal within the statutory 20-working-day response window; (2) file a first-level administrative complaint under Law on Administrative Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13 with the Director of the provincial DPI within 90 days from the rejection notice; (3) if dissatisfied, appeal to the Chairman of the Provincial People's Committee within 30 days after the first-level decision; or (4) initiate an administrative petition in the competent provincial People's Court within one year, with provision for interim suspension of the contested registration decision if irreparable harm is proven. A concurrently filed enterprise registration application may not be paired with a different name during the appeal; the applicant is advised to file the corrected name simultaneously while pursuing the complaint to avoid loss of filing priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered head office for a licensed commercial-litigation chamber under Enterprise Law 2020 and the law on legal services. The head-office address must be a physically accessible location in Viet Nam, evidenced by a lease agreement of at least 12 months, a lockable business unit, proper signage, and capacity to receive official notices and court service. A serviced office or co-working suite may be accepted if it has an independent desk/room, reception service, and a lease that is not a residential accommodation or mail-forwarding address. Virtual-office addresses do not satisfy the commercial-substance requirement for ISIC 6910 legal and litigation services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 25-30% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the DPI, licensing authority or taxation authority within the first 12 months after incorporation; the probability rises to above 60% if the UBO is later classified as a PEP, if a sanctions/PEP screening alert is generated, if registered-capital funding is unusual, or if the firm's client intake creates higher AML/CFT exposure for cross-border commercial litigation and asset tracing. Unannounced inspections may also follow interagency exchange with the State Bank of Viet Nam when the firm opens its IOLTA trust account.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprise No. 59/2020/QH14 (the "Enterprise Law 2020"), particularly Articles 29, 30, 31, 33 and 64 through 75; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, articles on market access and investment registration; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on business registration; and, for the specific legal-services scope, Law on Lawyers No. 20/2012/QH13 and Decree No. 123/2013/ND-CP.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office (Phòng Đăng ký kinh doanh), Department of Planning and Investment (Sở Kế hoạch và Đầu tư) of the province/city in Viet Nam where the LLC establishes its head office; national supervision by Agency for Business Registration, Ministry of Planning and Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Enterprise Registration Application (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp) in the form annexed to Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, together with the Company Charter, the List of Charter Members, and notarized legal-status copies of each member/investor.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital is prescribed for legal-services LLCs under the Enterprise Law 2020. Charter capital is fixed in the Charter and must be fully contributed within 90 days after the Enterprise Registration Certificate is issued; no escrow bank account is required as a matter of enterprise law, but the LLC must open a capital-contribution receipt and report contributions, and the foreign equity contribution must comply with the law on foreign exchange control. For legal-services activities, the Ministry of Justice may impose additional conditions on law-firm establishment and practising lawyers, including nationality, residency and academic qualification conditions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING MEMBERS OF [VN_LLC] (a limited liability company under Vietnamese law)

Adopted in writing on [date] by the sole/all founding member(s) of VN_LLC.

1. Capital Subscription: The founding members irrevocably subscribe to the full charter capital set out in the Company Charter, apportioned as stated in the List of Members. Each member shall contribute the amount opposite its/name in money and in accordance with the schedule. Contributions must be paid in full not later than 90 days from the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

2. Registered Office: The registered office and principal place of business shall be located at [full address in Viet Nam]. The Chairman of the Members' Council / legal representative is authorised to execute the office lease, obtain the landlord's assent, and file the registered-office declaration with the Business Registration Office.

3. Officers and Legal Representative: [Name, nationality, passport/ID] is appointed as Chairman of the Members' Council and legal representative of the company (as defined in Article 12 of the Enterprise Law 2020). The legal representative is authorised to sign the enterprise registration application, certify the Company Charter, open bank accounts, appoint service providers, and undertake all acts necessary to complete formation.

4. Governance and Licence: The Company Charter is adopted in final form. The legal representative is directed to apply for and obtain the legal-practice operating licence of the Ministry of Justice before commencing the regulated business line of cross-border commercial litigation and legal counselling.

5. Post-registration Instructions: The legal representative is authorised to procure a common seal, register tax with the General Department of Taxation, register electronic invoices, enrol social insurance, notify the seal sample on the national registration portal, and apply for fire-safety, occupational-safety and environmental clearances applicable to the office premises.

6. Effective Date and Binding Effect: This resolution takes effect immediately upon signature. Each member confirms that no conflicting resolution has been adopted and that this resolution binds the company and all members.

Signed by [Founding Member/Representative], [Name], [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Investment Clearance and Pre-formation Legal Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Single-Window Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) and the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the National Business Registration Portal to confirm the LLC's proposed Vietnamese and English name do not duplicate or infringe protected names. Confirm that business line ISIC 6910 (legal services / cross-border commercial litigation) is a conditional business line requiring a legal-practice licence. If the LLC has foreign equity, prepare the corresponding investment registration application and ensure that the legal-services activities satisfy WTO/market-access conditions applicable to foreign lawyers. If a foreign law-firm investor is involved, obtain the investment policy/registration certificate (IRC) before or in parallel with the enterprise registration, depending on the investor's nationality and treaty commitments.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (electronic form)
Draft Company Charter
List of proposed members/partners
Legal-status documents of each foreign corporate member (certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, apostilled/legalised)
Passport/ID and practising-lawyer certificate of each foreign lawyer who will manage the LLC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, amend the proposed name online and resubmit, or file a written complaint to the Director of the DPI within 30 days of the decision under the Law on Administrative Procedures. If the investment registration application is queried, supply supplementary documents within 30 business days; the competent authority must decide afresh, or appeal to the Department of Planning and Investment and ultimately the court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Department of Legal Service Administration; Fire Prevention, Fighting and Rescue Police of the provincial Public Security (C07)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application to establish the LLC as a licensed law company under the Law on Lawyers No. 20/2012/QH13 and Decree No. 123/2013/ND-CP. Ensure at least the required number of Managing Lawyers with valid practising certificates are engaged and that the office has premises acceptable to the Ministry of Justice. In parallel, file a fire-safety construction (design) dossier with the local Fire Police if the office is not automatically exempt; for a small 'office' in a certified building, obtain from the building owner the fire-safety acceptance certificate issued for the building and a tenant fit-out approval.
required_dossiers: Application for establishment/operation of a law company (law firm) (Form under Decree 123/2013/ND-CP)
Memorandum/Charter of the proposed law company
Decisions appointing Managing Lawyers and their practising certificates
Professional-liability insurance policy or alternative security (where required)
Certificate of capital contribution or bank balance confirmation (if licensed as a law company)
Office lease agreement, building title/tenancy schedule and landlord's occupancy certificate
Fire-safety design dossier or copy of building's fire-safety acceptance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Justice issues a supplementary request under Article 40 of Decree No. 123/2013/ND-CP, cure the deficiencies within the prescribed 30-day period. If the application is declined, file an administrative complaint with the Minister of Justice within 30 days, and thereafter a second-level complaint or administrative court petition. For fire-safety rejection, correct the non-compliance and reapply for inspection; re-inspection should be scheduled within 5 business days after confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Enterprise Registration Dossier and Issuance of Enterprise Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (Business Registration Office) via the National Business Registration Portal or direct counters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Enterprise Registration Application in the official form, annex the notarized Company Charter, List of Members, legal-status copies, and (for foreign-invested LLC) the Investment Registration Certificate and required professional licences. File on the National Single-Window Portal or in person; pay the official fee of 100,000 VND (approximately US$4.00). Within 3 working days after receiving a complete dossier, the DPI must issue the Enterprise Registration Certificate. Upon issuance, the ERC contains the enterprise code and tax code, and the LLC comes into existence as a legal person.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Application (Form No. I-1/XNDKND annexed to Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP)
Company Charter signed by each member/investor
List of Members (Form No. I-2/XNDKND)
Notarized copy of valid ID/passport (individuals) or legal incorporation certificate (corporate members)
Investment Registration Certificate (for foreign-invested LLC)
Licence of the Ministry of Justice for legal-services practice (when foreign or domestic legal practice is part of the business scope)
Written authorization and ID of the authorized MR/ERP submitting person (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI returns the dossier for correction, comply within 30 days; if no cure, re-file. If the DPI refuses, an administrative complaint may be lodged with the President of the Provincial People's Committee within 30 days, followed by judicial review in the Administrative Court. The 3-working-day rule is restored as soon as the supplemented dossier is re-submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Seal Creation and E-Invoice Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Department of Taxation (eTax/electronic portal); Public Security authorities for seal registration; Tax Sub-Department of the locality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 days after the ERC is issued, complete tax-registration revision/update with the local tax office using the enterprise tax code pre-coded in the ERC. Register for Corporate Income Tax, Value-Added Tax, and state 'license tax' obligations (exempt in the first calendar year). Design and engrave the company seal (if desired), and notify the seal sample in electronic form on the national portal. Apply for access to the Tax Authority's e-invoice system and subscribe electronic invoices for issuance. Arrange a bank account and declare it in tax registration, if available.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Tax registration declaration (Form 01/ĐK-TCT)
Identification of the legal representative
Information sheet on company seal (Form published by Ministry of Finance)
Evidence of office lease
Bank account details (after account opening)
Electronic invoice registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried, correct the declaration on the eTax portal and resubmit; late registration penalties may be waived if the error is cured before the deadline. If the seal sample is rejected, upload the corrected sample. Refusal decisions can be administratively appealed to the General Department of Taxation within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Capital Contribution and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks in Viet Nam (including joint-stock banks and approved foreign bank branches); Department of Planning and Investment for capital-contribution notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a transaction account and, if used, a capital-contribution account. Obtain from the bank a certificate of paid-in capital for each contribution. Ensure full contribution of charter capital is made within 90 days of the ERC date; thereafter submit the notice of capital contribution to DPI (including bank credit note/evidence) to update the registered capital status. Display at the office a signboard showing the registered enterprise name and code as per Decree No. 01/2021; retain the landlord's written lease consent for the registered address.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Enterprise Registration Certificate and Company Charter
Board/Members' Council resolution appointing signatories
Capital contribution transfer receipt / bank credit advice
Notice to DPI on fulfilment of capital contribution (Chứng nhận góp vốn or bank confirmation)
Office lease and landlord's consent / certificate of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the resolution, adopt a fresh Members' Council resolution with clear signatory powers. If capital is not contributed by the 90-day deadline, the LLC must (i) adjust charter capital and amend registration, or (ii) follow mandatory dissolution/revised contribution plan under Article 75 of the Enterprise Law 2020. Appeal or rectify with DPI by filing a 'Notice of Contribution Adjustment' before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Construction, Occupational Safety and Environmental Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Fire Prevention and Rescue Police; Department of Construction; Department of Natural Resources and Environment; Department of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs; local urban environmental service company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for and obtain final fire-safety acceptance for the office if the building floor does not already hold a certificate; register office construction/tenant fit-out with the Department of Construction where required. Complete an environmental self-registration if no full EIA is applicable under Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP and confirm the office's waste collection service with the local urban environmental company. Conduct occupational risk assessment, install first-aid station, fire extinguishers, emergency exit signs and an evacuation plan, and register workplace safety training. If the client file archive room exceeds floor-loading capacity, obtain structural inspection from a licensed engineering consultancy.
required_dossiers: Fire-safety acceptance/registration dossier (Decree 136/2020/ND-CP)
Occupancy permit/certificate of building completion issued by the competent construction authority
Landlord's copy of the building's fire-safety acceptance certificate
Environmental self-registration confirmation / municipal waste collection agreement
Occupational safety risk assessment report
Electrical installation inspection certificate
Floor-load calculation certificate (from registered surveyor if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire-safety authority refuses, correct physical defects and reapply for a second inspection; any refusal is subject to administrative appeal to the Provincial Police Director. Environmental registration rejection can be cured by filing updated Form P3? (environmental consolidation registration) with DONRE. Structure- and workplace safety deficiencies must be rectified within the time prescribed by the inspecting agency, with right of appeal to the Chief Inspector of Construction/Labour.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Justice – Department of Legal Service Administration (for law-company operating licence); Ministry of Planning and Investment / provincial DPI (for conditional investment and legal practice registration); Provincial Fire Prevention, Fighting and Rescue Police (for physical and operation safety).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Legal Practice Operating Licence / Law Company Establishment and Operation Licence issued under Law on Lawyers No. 20/2012/QH13 and Decree No. 123/2013/ND-CP; if the LLC will operate an international arbitration institution or an independent arbitral chamber, also the 'Arbitration Institute Establishment Licence' under the Law on Commercial Arbitration No. 54/2010/QH13 and Decree No. 64/2017/ND-CP.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) – Vietnam Environment Administration; provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) for local registration-level assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (low-risk administrative/professional services) – exempt from the statutory Full EIA Report requirement under Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP and Circular No. 02/2022/TT-BTNMT; the LLC is only required to carry out environmental self-registration with the communal/ward government or the urban environment company where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharge of domestic wastewater to municipal sewer must not impair the sewer network and must meet any parameters set by the urban drainage enterprise; if on-site treatment is performed before direct discharge to the environment, the treated effluent must comply with QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT (domestic wastewater technical regulation). There is no regulated industrial VOC emission source for an office of litigation counsel; where a standby diesel generator is installed, stack emissions must satisfy QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT (industrial emissions) and fuel storage must be less than the hazardous-waste threshold. Solid waste including confidential legal files should be segregated; hazardous waste generated if any (e.g., printer cartridges, batteries) must be declared and shipped to a licensed waste handler under the Environmental Protection Law 2020 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain Fire Prevention and Fighting Safety Acceptance (Certificate of Fire Safety Acceptance or, for simple premises, a written confirmation/commitment) under Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP and ensure office evacuation planning, smoke detectors and portable extinguishers are in place. Structural load: confirm building completion certificate/occupancy permit and, if storing massive paper/file archives, a structural load assessment by a registered civil engineer. Occupational safety: train staff, conduct periodical safety inspections, arrange first aid, and register high-risk equipment (if any) under the Labor Code and Decree No. 44/2016/ND-CP. The LLC shall also be listed in the office building's fire evacuation plan and comply with the civil-defense and rescue coordination requirements of the local Fire Police.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation of Vietnam (Tong Cuc Thue, Ministry of Finance). Primary portals: National Business Registration Portal (Dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn), National e-Tax Portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn), and National e-Invoice Portal (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn). Provincial-level administration is carried out by the municipal/provincial Tax Department (Cuc Thue) where the LLC's head office is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) or the relevant Export Processing/Industrial Zone Authority, supported by the foreign investor's incorporation documents and legalization of signature. Step 2: File the Enterprise Registration Dossier through the National Business Registration Portal to obtain the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); the business tax identification number (Ma so thue, MST) is automatically and simultaneously issued by the tax authority upon ERC approval, integrated with the national tax infrastructure. Step 3: Complete post-licensing tax identity setup at the provincial Tax Department, including electronic tax registration (Form 08-DK-TCT prefill), bank account disclosure, e-Tax account activation, and digital certificate (token) registration for e-filing. Step 4: Register the e-invoice account with the General Department of Taxation (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn) and apply for the use of e-invoices with tax authority codes; this registration is mandatory before issuing the first 0% VAT export invoice. Step 5: For a foreign-invested LLC, no separate VAT ID is needed; the MST serves as the unified TIN for CIT, VAT, customs (in certain schemes), social insurance, and e-invoice purposes. Step 6: If the LLC simultaneously operates as a customs declarant, obtain a customs code and register bank guarantee accounts with the General Department of Customs; this is auxiliary to the tax identity. No passport of TIN is required; the procedure is fully digital and typically completed within 15 working days of IRC issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A foreign-invested LLC incorporated under the Law on Enterprises is per se a Vietnamese-resident enterprise under the Law on Enterprise Income Tax (CIT Law No. 14/2008/QH12, as amended by Law No. 32/2013/QH13). It is taxed on worldwide income and has no pass-through eligibility; profits are subject to CIT at the 20% standard rate plus a 0% dividend withholding tax for non-resident shareholders remitting dividends out of Vietnam. The LLC is not a transparent entity, and no partnership-style pass-through is recognized for tax purposes. Territorial scope: for a resident enterprise, export services rendered to foreign clients are taxable at 0% CIT? No, they are taxable to CIT as ordinary income; the territorial classification is irrelevant inside the CIT net. However, the 0% VAT export regime (detailed in indirect taxation) applies. For inbound non-resident service providers, a separate Foreign Contractor Tax regime applies, which is not applicable to this locally incorporated LLC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam does not administer a US-style 'check-the-box' classification election; all LLCs are per se CIT-resident entities. Statutory elections and formal mechanisms that are available and relevant: (1) Fiscal year election: the company may elect a calendar-year accounting period (default) or an approved fiscal year ending 31 March, 30 June, or 30 September (must file notice with tax authority). (2) VAT credit method election: where annual revenue from sale of goods/services is below 1 billion VND (approximately USD 40,000), the taxpayer may elect either the credit method or the direct method; once the credit method is elected or revenue exceeds the threshold, the credit method is mandatory. (3) Loss carry-forward election: the taxpayer may elect to carry forward CIT losses (no carryback) for an uninterrupted period of up to 5 years. (4) Deduction of actual R&D expenditure: an election exists to apply a special cap (10% of annual taxable income) for certain R&D costs (Law on Technology Transfer), although not relevant to a litigation practice. (5) Fixed-asset depreciation method election: taxpayers may elect straight-line, declining-balance, or unit-of-production depreciation per Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC, subject to consistency requirements. (6) Foreign exchange difference election: eligible dates for FX revaluation may be selected within the CIT declaration cycle. (7) Hybrid mismatch arrangements: no elective opt-out exists; Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (transfer pricing and BEPS Action 2) mandatorily disallows deductions for hybrid mismatch transactions that result in double non-taxation or double deduction. There is no separate 'hybrid mismatch election' prescribed in Vietnamese law; the rule is mandatory and enforced through transfer-pricing documentation. Group consolidation of tax losses is not permitted; each LLC files standalone CIT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.mandatory_statutory_reference: Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 (effective 1 July 2020), Decree 126/2020/ND-CP (implementation of tax administration), Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC (e-invoicing and e-tax filing), Decree 123/2020/ND-CP, Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC, Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / GTGT) established under Law No. 13/2008/QH12 on Value Added Tax, substantially amended by Law No. 106/2016/QH13, implemented by Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC, Circular 119/2014/TT-BTC, and Decree 123/2020/ND-CP on electronic invoices. Taxable supply nexus is territorial: VAT applies to goods and services used/supplied in Vietnam, regardless of the location of the supplier. A cross-border legal service is deemed exported only if it is provided to a foreign organization or foreign individual and consumed entirely outside Vietnam.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For an LLC: no registration threshold exists — VAT registration, invoicing, and periodic filing obligations commence on the date of Enterprise Registration Certificate issuance irrespective of turnover. For sole proprietorships/household businesses (not applicable to LLC), a 100,000,000 VND per annum threshold applies. Because this entity is an LLC performing export-exempt? No, the entity performs legal services at 10% standard rate domestically and 0% for exported services, therefore it falls under the credit method and cannot elect the direct method if annual turnover is or is expected to be above 1 billion VND (the statutory credit-method threshold per Article 11, Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC). The company must also obtain a tax-authority-code e-invoice sequence even when producing 0% export invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices (including 0% export invoices) must be electronic invoices per Decree 123/2020/ND-CP, generated by a certified software application and transmitted to the General Department of Taxation's e-invoice portal (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn). Two regimes exist: (A) E-invoices with tax-authority codes (most common for new enterprises): each invoice is transmitted in real-time to the GDT portal, which affixes a digital authentication code (ma cua co quan thue) and returns the encrypted code instantly; the invoice is deemed cleared for fiscal purposes only upon receipt of this code. This is, in effect, an electronic clearance/stamping mandate. The API integration is supported through licensed e-invoice service providers (CENs) that interface with the GDT's centralized system. (B) E-invoices without tax-authority codes: permitted for certain internal-use cases or for enterprises meeting technical conditions (digital signature, periodic transmission, and stricter pre-issuance validation), but not recommended for an active exporter due to higher audit risk. Mandatory fields include the 0% VAT rate indicator and the reason code for VAT exemption, if applicable (Article 91). Invoices must be transmitted to the tax authority's archive within 1 working day of issuance? For coded e-invoices the data is transmitted in real-time; other invoice data must be transferred through the vendor portal not later than the 15th of the month following the invoicing period. XML/JSON schema, digital signature of seller (using registered token), and the GDT's assigned invoice series are mandatory. There is no separate physical stamp; the tax authority code operates as the digital stamp. Since July 2022, all transactions (including services of a litigation chamber) must be e-invoiced; paper invoices are rejected for input VAT credit and are treated as unissued from a fiscal standpoint.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Legal services provided by a Vietnamese LLC to a foreign client qualify for the 0% VAT rate if, and only if, the following cumulative statutory conditions under Article 9, Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC are satisfied: (1) the service recipient is a foreign organization registered in a foreign country or a foreign individual residing overseas; (2) the service is consumed entirely outside Vietnam — for cross-border commercial litigation and multi-jurisdictional arbitration, this is evidenced by contractual governing law (non-Vietnamese), the venue/seat of arbitration or litigation (outside Vietnam), and delivery of legal advice/representation outputs to a foreign addressee; (3) the service is not in the exclusion list (legal services are not excluded; exclusions concern natural resources, telecommunications, transport, insurance, banking, and services in taxable zones); (4) the foreign client pays in a convertible foreign currency via a Vietnamese licensed bank; (5) the Vietnam LLC holds a full export service contract and a payment receipt/remittance record; (6) the e-invoice shows 0% VAT and contains the contract number and foreign-currency amount; and (7) the LLC has submitted an export declared/using list (Bang ke hoa don dich vu xuat khau) along with the supporting contract and the foreign client's registration/license certificate to the tax authority. Export zero-rating is not optional; if the economic substance test fails, the service is subject to 10% VAT on the invoiced amount plus penalties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (only for physical goods; for pure cross-border litigation/arbitration services, no customs declaration is filed — the controlling substitute is the export service contract and the List of Exported Service Invoices (Phu luc Bang ke 01/GTGT)).

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (applicable only to incidental physical exhibits, evidence files, or hearing documents; for services, the equivalent evidence is the documented date-stamped delivery of legal memoranda, court/arbitral filings, and hearing attendance records performed outside Vietnam).

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC): official certificate issued by an authorized Vietnamese commercial bank evidencing receipt and conversion? or receipt of foreign currency from the foreign client, showing the matching invoice number and contract reference; at minimum, the bank statement showing the cross-border receipt without domestic intermediation.

Export service contract in a legally valid form, containing: place of performance, governing law clause (foreign law), fee schedule in a freely convertible foreign currency, and dispute resolution venue outside Vietnam.
Zero-rated e-invoice with tax-authority code transmitted to the GDT portal, stating 0% VAT and referencing the export contract number.
Foreign client's certificate of registration/license issued by its home jurisdiction (translated and legalized if requested), used to verify the non-resident status of the recipient.

Detailed work logs / deliverables register (advices, court filings, briefs, memoranda, invoices) demonstrating that the service was actually rendered and completed outside Vietnam and not used within Vietnam.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The General Department of Taxation and Customs combined enforcement framework authorizes retrospective VAT clawback for export zero-rating fraud or misdeclaration. If the 0% rate is denied, the tax authority will reassess 10% VAT on the full invoice amount, impose a late-payment interest charge at 0.05% per day (approximately 18.25% per annum) computed from the original due date to the payment date, and apply administrative penalties per Decree 125/2020/ND-CP: (a) underdeclaration: penalty equal to 20% of the additional tax assessed; (b) taxable-amount understatement with no fraud: 20% plus full interest; (c) fraudulent evasion: penalty of 1.0 to 3.0 times the evaded VAT amount, with possible criminal referral under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 (amended 2017) if evaded tax exceeds 100,000,000 VND (approximately USD 4,000) and other statutory elements are met, carrying up to 7 years' imprisonment, a fine up to 4,500,000,000 VND, and prohibition from holding office/business activity for up to 5 years; (d) issuance of false invoices: Article 203 penalties up to 20 years' imprisonment for invoice crimes; (e) corporate offenders may face suspension of e-invoice issuance authority, temporary closure of the head-office address, revocation of the tax code in extreme cases, and removal from the 'good taxpayer' green channel and customs priority regime. Retrospective clawback periods: 5 years for unintentional underdeclaration (General Tax Administration Law 38/2019/QH14, Article 8?) and 10 years for fraud/evasion, extending to a full supply-chain audit of supporting documentation, foreign remittance records, and correspondence proving the offshore consumption of legal services. Legal-entity representatives (General Director/CEO) are jointly and severally liable, and will be named in criminal proceedings for fraudulent zero-rating schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV; Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam), the sole monetary authority and foreign-exchange regulator, acting under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam No. 46/2010/QH12 (as amended in 2017) and the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 (as amended by Ordinance No. 04/2013/UBTVQH13). The binding implementing instruments for treasury operations are: (i) Circular No. 06/2019/TT-NHNN governing foreign-exchange management for foreign direct investment (FDI), current transactions, Direct Investment Capital Accounts, and profit remittance; (ii) Circular No. 02/2021/TT-NHNN replacing Circular No. 15/2015/TT-NHNN, governing spot, forward, swap, and option foreign-exchange transactions between authorized banks and corporate customers; and (iii) Circular No. 23/2014/TT-NHNN, as amended by Circular No. 02/2019/TT-NHNN, governing payment-account opening and customer identification (KYC/eKYC). Administrative FX sanctions are imposed under Decree No. 88/2019/ND-CP, as amended by Decree No. 143/2021/ND-CP, with fines up to VND 200 million and forced-conversion orders for repatriation breaches.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vietnamese đồng (VND) is not fully convertible. Current-account transactions are de facto convertible upon documentary verification by an authorized bank: a foreign-invested law firm may freely receive and pay overseas legal fees, arbitrator invoices, expert-witness costs, court charges, and arbitration-institution fees, provided the underlying engagement contract, invoice, and tax compliance documents are filed with the servicing bank. Capital-account transactions, by contrast, are restricted: equity injection must pass through a registered Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA); shareholder loans with a term above one year must be registered with the SBV; and profit remittance is permitted only after the annual audited financial statements are completed, the corporate income tax finalization obligation is settled, and a board resolution on dividend distribution is executed. For a litigation-services LLC, remittance of fees received from foreign clients is classified as an export of services (current account) and enjoys full convertibility, but a bank will require an export-services statement, the signed retainer, and an invoice to evidence the economic substance of the cross-border service provision. Profit distribution to a foreign parent is subject to a further condition that the LLC has no accumulated losses and has set off all prior-year losses against taxable income, as certified by the tax authority; the remittance itself attracts no Vietnamese withholding tax when the CIT finalization obligation is satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory percentage surrender of export-proceeds foreign currency to VND; the statutory surrender regime was abolished in 2012. However, all export proceeds — including cross-border legal, arbitration, asset-tracing, and expert advisory services — must be repatriated to Vietnam within 90 days from the date of service completion (for goods, 180 days, extendable to 360 days with prior bank approval). The proceeds must be credited to a foreign-currency demand account or sold immediately to an authorized bank; retention of unrepatriated export proceeds abroad is an administrative violation. For a litigation chamber, proceeds earned by the foreign-litigation team (e.g., hourly fees billed from a foreign database or paid into an offshore collections account) must nevertheless flow back to the VN_LLC operating account within the 90-day window. Non-compliance triggers penalties under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP (as amended by Decree 143/2021/ND-CP), including fines up to VND 200 million, suspension of foreign-exchange activities, and an SBV order compelling the sale of foreign currency; criminal prosecution under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 14/2022/QH15 may also apply where the non-repatriation is used to conceal ownership of recovered arbitration awards.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) for inbound equity; VND operational account; USD/EUR demand accounts for FX retention; segregated client-funds escrow sub-account for arbitration award proceeds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account; VND current account; foreign-currency clearing account; treasury sweep arrangement for demand deposits

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account; VND current account; custody/deposit-for-expenses (ký quỹ) account; strong escrow and guarantee product suite for attachment of arbitration security

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for the primary trust/IOLTA clearing rail; Medium for ancillary collection sub-ledgers. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currencycloud, MultiPass) are not licensed as banks by the SBV and may not lawfully hold VND, open client-funds escrow accounts, or settle arbitration awards on behalf of a Vietnamese-licensed law firm. Under Decree No. 101/2012/ND-CP (as amended by Decree No. 80/2016/ND-CP) and Circular No. 39/2014/TT-NHNN, only licensed payment intermediaries may process non-cash payments in Vietnam; EMIs must contractually route through a licensed Vietnamese commercial bank, and the bank remains the account-holding institution of record. Consequently, an EMI may be used as an overseas receivables sub-ledger for invoice-to-invoice matching of foreign client fees, but the operative clearing rail and all client-funds custody must be held at an authorized bank within Vietnam. Legal consequence of using an unlicensed EMI as principal rail: the account relationship is voidable, export-proceeds repatriation obligations are breached, and the firm risks tax authority challenge on invoicing substance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence is the prevailing practice for a foreign-invested LLC: the legal representative (Chairman of the Members' Council or the General Director) must appear in person at the bank's head office or major branch in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City for an in-person KYC interview, presenting original passports, the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), the Law Practice License, the Bar Association certificate of the responsible partner, a board resolution on account opening, and the authority matrix of authorized signatories. Remote opening (eKYC) is formally permitted for low-risk individual clients under Circular 02/2019/TT-NHNN, but for corporate professional-services entities the market treats the interview as mandatory. If the legal representative is offshore, the bank will accept a notarized, consular-legalized power of attorney designating a Vietnam-based director or the law firm's office manager to appear, provided the principal's identity documents are authenticated and the POA is registered in the firm's corporate file at the Department of Planning and Investment; in practice, at least one foreign UBO or the Vietnamese managing partner must still sit for a video-interview with the bank's compliance officer before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IOLTA/client-funds account classification gap: Vietnamese payment-account regulations do not recognize an 'IOLTA' or 'lawyers trust account' as a distinct statutory account species; banks applying strict SBV rules may classify an escrow fund as a hybrid 'custody deposit' or 'deposit for expenses' account, raising refusal or recharacterization risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) A notarized copy of the Law Practice License issued by the Ministry of Justice under the Law on Lawyers No. 65/2006/QH11 (amended 2012); (2) a Board resolution defining the client-funds account as a segregated escrow capable of holding litigation proceeds; (3) a client-funds holding policy compliant with Article 25 of the Law on Lawyers and the Vietnam Bar Federation's Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics (2019), demonstrating no commingling with operating funds; (4) a sample client engagement letter with an express waiver of interest and an instruction that awarded sums pass through the segregated sub-account; (5) a weekly reconciliation template, with an undertaking to produce the register on SBV demand; and (6) confirmation that the bank's own 'custody deposit' internal product code (e.g., product code 08 or equivalent) is accepted as the booking vehicle for the underlying arbitration award.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: the 25% look-through requirement under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 14/2022/QH15 and Decree No. 48/2024/ND-CP obliges the bank to identify every natural person UBO; foreign silent partners, discretionary family trusts, and litigation-funding backers behind the LLC are classic red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Full corporate registry extract of the LLC with the shareholder register; (2) a manually executed UBO declaration table showing each natural person holding above 25%, with passport copies and residential-address proof; (3) source-of-wealth declaration for each UBO covering the initial capital contribution, corroborated by bank statements or audited financial statements of the source entity; (4) where litigation-funding or third-party funding exists, the funding agreement, the funder's KYC pack, and a legal-memorandum certifying that the funding is legitimate and does not constitute an unlicensed lending activity under Vietnam's civil code; and (5) authorization for the bank to inspect the national enterprise database (Đăng ký quốc gia) to confirm no mismatch with the submitted UBO list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically-exposed-persons (PEP) exposure: cross-border commercial litigation frequently involves parties residing in or linked to sanctioned jurisdictions, or state-owned enterprises from high-risk jurisdictions, triggering UN Security Council, OFAC, EU, and SBV-issued watch-list screening; an automatic hit will freeze the account and generate a report to the SBV AML Division.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) A documented sanctions/PEP screening policy with a clear client-onboarding matrix; (2) negative sanctions clear-sheet certificates produced by an independent screening vendor for each matter, including the adverse-party and the counterparty's counsel; (3) the managing partner's 'lawyer's non-engagement certificate' confirming that no client receives settlement proceeds for the benefit of a designated person; (4) a transaction-monitoring protocol committing the firm to a 24-hour SBV notification under Article 42 of the AML Law should a client become sanctioned mid-matter; and (5) the escrow agreement clause prohibiting settlement disbursements to any entity on the EU/OFC/UN consolidated lists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Status Report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động của doanh nghiệp) attaching audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via the National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the calendar fiscal year (on or before 31 March of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 10,000,000–20,000,000 (approx. USD 400–800) under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; failure to file for 6 consecutive months while not operating triggers administrative strike-off (revocation) of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax finalization return (Form 02/TNDN) with supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Sub-Department of the General Department of Taxation at the registered head-office province
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the calendar fiscal year (on or before 31 March of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the outstanding tax amount; administrative penalty up to 100% of the under-declared tax under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; criminal prosecution for intentional tax evasion above statutory thresholds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements submitted to the enterprise registration and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) and the provincial Tax Sub-Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the calendar fiscal year (on or before 31 March); independent audit must be completed before CIT finalization filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine for late submission under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP and Decree 122/2021/ND-CP, escalating on repeat violations; certificate revocation possible for persistent non-compliance; the audit must be rendered by a licensed Vietnamese independent auditing firm.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to all foreign-invested enterprises (FDI LLCs) irrespective of revenue, asset, or headcount thresholds under Article 15 of the Law on Independent Audit No. 67/2013/QH13 and Decree 17/2012/ND-CP; also mandatory for public companies, credit institutions, insurers, and securities firms.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS) promulgated under Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements of qualifying groups and for financial reporting under international investment covenants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 14/2022/QH14 and Decree No. 09/2023/ND-CP, the LLC must refresh ultimate beneficial ownership identification data at least once every 12 months for ongoing business relationships; any shareholding transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members within 7 days and UBO identification re-performed before the transfer is registered; Vietnam maintains no public UBO registry, but complete UBO records must be available on demand to the State Bank of Vietnam and competent law-enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members with capital contribution amounts and voting rights
Register of Directors / Legal Representative and Controllers
Minute Book of Members' Resolutions and Shareholding Transfer Approvals
Ultimate Beneficial Owner and AML/KYC identification files

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–2,000 per annum for registered office address, corporate secretarial, and compliance agent services in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–8,000 per annum for licensed independent audit of a medium-sized FDI litigation-services LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax rate 20% for all LLCs under Law No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended. Preferential rates: 10% for 15 years for qualified high-tech, software, and large-scale manufacturing projects; 17%/20% for investments in eligible geographical areas or sectors. Tax holidays: exemption for up to 4 years and 50% reduction for up to 9 subsequent years in qualifying industries/locations. Foreign-invested LLCs in commercial litigation services (ISIC 6910) generally do not qualify for sector-based incentives absent special investment zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT finalization declaration Form 03/TNDN issued under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC; submitted electronically via the Viet Nam electronic tax portal (https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) or the national Tax Administration e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual finalization; quarterly provisional CIT prepayments with estimated declarations filed every quarter.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual finalization return due within 90 calendar days from the fiscal year-end; for December year-end LLC this is 31 March of the following year. Quarterly provisional CIT declarations and payments are due by the 30th day after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period and fiscal year-end date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested LLC must record the approved fiscal year (normally calendar year) in the format DD/MM/YYYY to YYYY.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification (MST) and registered name and address of the LLC
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Vietnamese tax identification number issued to the LLC; do not enter the foreign parent's overseas tax ID here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from goods and services subject to CIT (net of VAT)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report total Vietnamese-source gross revenue for legal and arbitration services, including service fees, litigation success fees, and retained amounts, in Vietnamese Dong (VND). Cross-border fee income attributable to Viet Nam must be included.

Claim only documented expenses incurred in generating Vietnamese-source revenue. Deductions must satisfy Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC; expenses paid to related offshore parties require transfer pricing documentation and are subject to the 30% EBITDA interest cap.
Computed as net revenue less allowable deductions plus non-deductible expenses and before loss set-off limited to 5 years. Related-party adjustments and transfer pricing changes must be reflected.
Insert 20% for standard LLC; if a valid investment registration certificate granted a preferential rate (10%-17%), attach the certificate and enter the applicable percentage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable or overpayment after offset of quarterly provisional payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident LLC must reconcile cumulative quarterly prepayments against final annual liability; the difference must be paid with the finalization return. Overpayments may be offset or refunded under the Tax Administration Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP range from VND 2,000,000 for up to 5 days of delay to VND 25,000,000 for delays beyond 90 days. Late payment of tax attracts statutory daily interest of 0.03% on the unpaid amount. Non-filing after formal written demand may be reclassified as tax evasion attracting a penalty of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax and criminal sanction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Viet Nam does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax on after-tax profit distributions from an LLC to its non-resident shareholder. The distributed profit is subject only to the 20% CIT already paid at the entity level. Remittance of profits abroad is otherwise unrestricted provided tax obligations are fully settled.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Viet Nam levies no dividend withholding tax, DTA dividend relief is not required for LLC profit distributions. For categories still subject to Vietnamese source withholding tax (interest, royalties, technical service fees), the foreign beneficial owner must file the DTA reduction/exemption dossier with the Vietnamese payer before the payment date, attaching a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority, the treaty relief application form annexed to Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC, evidence of beneficial ownership, and underlying contracts. The Vietnamese payer applies the treaty rate and retains the dossier. If the TRC is obtained after the due date, a refund claim may be filed via the tax administration within the statutory statute of limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) rates: interest paid to non-resident lenders: 5%; royalties, software license fees, and technology transfer payments: 10%. Under Viet Nam's income tax treaties (OECD/UN model based), the standard treaty rate for royalties and interest is frequently 10%, and certain treaties reduce interest to 5% or exempt it. Treaty relief requires a valid TRC and beneficial ownership confirmation. The payer is liable for withholding and remitting the tax to the Vietnamese tax authority.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 30,000,000,000 (VND 30 billion) aggregate annual related-party transaction value; taxpayers with total annual revenue below VND 50,000,000,000 and related-party transactions below VND 30,000,000,000 may qualify for exemption from preparing the Local File and Master File. Related-party transaction declarations (Forms 01, 02 and 03) are made on the annual CIT finalization Form 03/TNDN package under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Viet Nam has not enacted a standalone Economic Substance Regulation statute of the style used in Mauritius or the BVI, but the Law on Tax Administration (No. 38/2019/QH14) and Decree 132/2020/ND-CP introduce a General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance over form. Arrangements lacking commercial rationale, personnel, premises, and risk-bearing functions will be recharacterized and disregarded. Thin capitalization rules apply: net interest expenses, including related and third-party debt, are deductible only up to 30% of EBITDA for CIT purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Vietnamese-source revenue from cross-border litigation services, using fictitious VAT invoices for disbursements, or inflating deductible expenses through shell vendors; also concealing fee-sharing arrangements with offshore cooperating counsel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax amount under the Law on Tax Administration; late payment interest 0.03% per day; criminal liability under Article 200 of the Penal Code with fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment of up to 7 years when the evaded amount reaches VND 100,000,000 or more.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and managing directors who ordered or knowingly facilitated the evasion are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax; criminal penalties apply personally. The tax authority may impose an exit ban (travel hold) preventing directors from leaving Viet Nam during investigation and collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Vietnamese LLC with no employees, no real office, no separate bank account or operative trust account, and routing litigation or arbitration fees through the entity to shift profits from a foreign law firm and claim Vietnamese preferential tax treatment or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the structure, disallowance of the entity's invoices and deductions, additional CIT at 20% plus late interest, fines for false registration up to VND 1,000,000,000, and potential revocation of the enterprise registration certificate under Article 216 of the Law on Enterprise if the entity is found to be a facade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the unpaid tax following piercing of the corporate veil; courts can order restitution of assets transferred out; the State Bank and tax authorities coordinate to impose travel bans; imprisonment is possible under fraud and tax evasion provisions when criminal intent is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and IOLTA Trust Account Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LLC's IOLTA-style client trust account to move non-client funds, commingle settlement proceeds with operating income, or facilitate payments for unnamed beneficial owners without conducting CDD/KYC under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to VND 200,000,000 per AML violation, mandatory reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit (State Bank), temporary suspension of the legal-services license, seizure of suspect account balances, and criminal money-laundering penalties under Article 324 of the Penal Code including fines of up to VND 3,000,000,000 and imprisonment up to 15 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors and compliance officers are subject to personal criminal accountability for structured transactions; travel bans are commonly used; directors can be held civilly liable to harmed trust-account beneficiaries; professional liability insurance is void; directors may be disqualified from serving as bank signatories or anti-money-laundering compliance officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Violations and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exercising management and control in Viet Nam but shifting profits to a related offshore entity through non-arm's length mark-ups on legal fees, without preparing Local File/Master File despite crossing the VND 30 billion related-party transaction or the VND 50 billion revenue thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority restating taxable income by applying an arm's length method, additional CIT at 20%, late payment interest, administrative penalties of 1 to 3 times the evaded amount for material misstatement, and fines of up to VND 100,000,000 for failure to submit required transfer pricing forms and documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing declarations are personally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties; criminal tax evasion liability under Article 200 of the Penal Code may follow if the corrected tax exceeds statutory thresholds; an exit ban may remain in force until the assessment is paid.
